rationale: The buyer is a specific, nameable role — an engineering lead or CTO at a SaaS startup already paying $200–$5k/month in LLM API costs — who demonstrably loses real money to this problem (the source post cites a $1,860 overage). Willingness to pay is credible because they're already paying for LLM APIs and adjacent APM tools (Datadog, Sentry), so a $49–$99/month add-on is in-budget. The autonomy gate is marginal at 7: after onboarding (which requires the customer to drop in a lightweight SDK or set up a proxy), monitoring, alerting, and billing can be fully automated — but initial integration requires some per-customer setup work, which nudges it to the floor. The build_gate for operational_autonomy is exactly met (7 = min), so the stage is validated rather than capped, but it's borderline and the validation should confirm whether customers will self-serve the integration without hand-holding.
solution_plan: WHAT: A lightweight LLM cost-monitoring SaaS — a drop-in proxy/middleware layer that sits between a team's app and the OpenAI/Anthropic API, tags every call with a feature label, and fires a Slack or email alert when per-feature spend crosses a configurable threshold. BUILD: The factory builds a simple HTTP proxy using a Claude-generated script (no custom infra — it's a thin reverse proxy with a Postgres cost log), a one-page dashboard served as a static site, a Stripe payment link for $49/month, and an onboarding email sequence. The operator does not write code; the factory handles the prompt engineering, config, and deployment scripts. SELL: Target engineering leads and CTOs at AI-enabled SaaS startups via dev.to, Hacker News 'Show HN', and Twitter/X AI-dev communities — these audiences self-select and the source post proves they exist and are vocal. Outreach copy goes into the approval queue before any message is sent. MAINTAIN: Incoming proxy traffic, cost attribution, and alert emails all run via the code + Claude; new customer onboarding is a self-serve Stripe checkout → automated API key provisioning → welcome email. The operator's only recurring touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing the weekly cost digest. NOTE: Before building, run a 1-week validation: post a 'would you pay $49/month for this?' landing page to 2–3 dev forums and require 10 email sign-ups. The integration friction (SDK drop-in vs proxy) is the key risk to resolve.
notes: operational_autonomy is exactly at the build_gate floor (7). Buildability is 6 (meets gate) but the proxy + dashboard is more than a pure prompt — it needs a deployed HTTP service. Validate whether customers will self-serve the SDK integration before investing in infrastructure. No penalties applied; product is legitimate and fully aligned with platform TOS.
